notes.text: December Tokyo: cold, and dark well before you reach dinner. Pack a warm layer in your carry-on, not buried in a suitcase.
Load a Welcome Suica on every phone at Haneda, and keep yen cash on you: Mutekiya takes nothing else.
Original passports out tonight: the drinking age is 20 and Round1 can card you. Tomorrow you leave at 07:20, so the ramen is the finish line.

stops.summary: Land 15:00, clear immigration, put a Welcome Suica on every phone before the Keikyu gates.
stops.story: You land at 15:00 and the clock starts now. The whole first evening runs on trains, so the one job at Haneda is making sure eight phones tap through the gates without a single person stuck behind the barrier digging for coins.
how: Immigration and bags, then regroup before the train gates.
Set up and load Welcome Suica on every phone; load enough for a few days.
Keikyu Airport line to Shinagawa, JR Yamanote to Ikebukuro, Seibu Ikebukuro line to Higashi-Nagasaki, then walk with the bags.
tips: Everything comes with you to Ninja House: it stays there until Dec 18, so no luggage-forwarding today.
Decline any card terminal that offers to charge you in USD; pay in yen.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Dump every suitcase, grab passports and cash, and be on the 18:12 Seibu train to Ikebukuro.
stops.story: Ninja House is base camp until Dec 18, so unpack properly once and stop thinking about luggage. Then straight back out: dinner is already waiting in Ikebukuro.
how: Check in (from 16:00) and drop all the suitcases.
Walk to Higashi-Nagasaki for the Seibu Ikebukuro line 18:12 → Ikebukuro 18:17, ¥170; 24 min door to door.
tips: Running late? A taxi is 12 min to Ikebukuro.
wishes: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)

stops.summary: Night one: all-you-can-eat wagyu and nomihodai in a private room built for exactly eight.
stops.story: A wagyu all-you-can-eat specialist a minute from JR Ikebukuro, with a private room for 6–8 that fits the eight of you with zero spare chairs. You grill, they keep the plates coming, the drinks plan does the rest; it is the welcome speech nobody has to give. Highly rated on Google and a 2026 Xiaohongshu favourite for value.
how: Ask for the private room (個室) under your booking for 8 (8名・個室).
Pick the course: ¥3,190, ¥4,290 or ¥7,590 pp, then add nomihodai.
Pace yourselves: Round1 is next, an 8 min walk away.
tips: Book online through Hot Pepper or Gurunavi for points and coupons, 3–4 weeks ahead for mid-December.
The 80-item course at ¥3,190 is the value play; the top course is the flex.
Check the booking confirmation actually says private room, not just a table for 8.
stops.booking: Check it is booked: Hot Pepper, Gurunavi or 03-6709-1973, private room for 8 (8名・個室)
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: Two lanes of four, one bowling grudge match, then arcade chaos until you get hungry again.
stops.story: Round1 Ikebukuro never closes: bowling, karaoke, billiards, darts and table tennis run all night in one building. Split into two teams of four, make the losing lane buy the ramen, and settle any rematch on the arcade floor.
how: Get two lanes of four at the counter and ask what night packs they have.
After bowling, hit the arcade floor before it shuts at 00:50.
If the night demands it, grab a karaoke room; otherwise walk to Mutekiya, 8 min.
tips: Carry passports: some Round1 night rules turn away under-20s.
Lanes can be reserved on the Round1 site if you want zero waiting.
Budget about ¥3,000 pp, but check the price table at the counter: night packs vary by store.
stops.booking: Walk in, or reserve lanes on the Round1 site
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.summary: Midnight tonkotsu at Ikebukuro's late-night ramen legend, then the last Seibu train home.
stops.story: Mutekiya pours rich tonkotsu-shoyu with thick chashu until the small hours, which is why so much of Ikebukuro ends up here after drinks. Counter only, no tables, so you eat in waves and wave at each other through the steam.
how: Queue together outside; 2026 reviews put the wait at 10 to 30 minutes.
Order the honmaru (¥1,150); extra noodles are ¥200.
Expect to be seated a few at a time, not side by side.
Out by 00:00 for the Seibu train 00:18 → Higashi-Nagasaki 00:23, ¥170.
tips: Kaedama (extra noodles) is the move if bowling made you hungry again.
Miss the train? Two taxis, 12 min home.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
